title: rapid-retainer-triage-slate-sep2026
body:
Context:
This is a working triage and cut-slate for a small, focused sprint were calling the "retainer" lift: quick structural improvements to the Console route/model routing UX that unblock Dedicated/Private customers asking for safer rollouts and cheaper steady-state ops. Not a feature-complete ship; goal is incremental value + low-risk rollout hooks.

Meeting notes (2026-09-02):
- Attendees: Ava, Ravi, Lin, Priya, Marco. 40m sync.
- Goal: reduce the top-10 routing incidents and make model pin + fallback explicit in the route edit flow.
- Consensus: prioritize a small set of UI affordances + server-side flagging to allow safe canary + auto-fallback for overloaded GPUs.

Problem statement: 
- Users cannot easily preset per-route fallback policies (model variant, region fallback, degrade-to-hosted).
- Debugging a failed rollout requires jumping between Console, Logs, and Model Catalog.
- Lack of roll-trips (tripwires) causes teams to keep conservative model pins, increasing cost.

Proposed scope (sprint-length, 2 weeks):
1) Route edit UX: 
   - New compact "Fallbacks & Rollouts" panel in route settings (wireframe notes below).
   - Quick toggle: "Allow automatic fallback" (default off for Private).
   - Dropdown: "Fallback chain" with up to 3 entries: model-variant -> region -> hosted.
2) Model pin quicktoggle: 
   - Inline pin selector on the route list row (hover reveal).
   - Confirmation modal showing cost delta and recent perf delta.
3) Rollout tripwire: 
   - Server flag + Console checkbox to enable an automatic rollback if error rate > 3% in 5m.
4) Observability links: 
   - Add one-click links to last 3 failed requests for a route (jump to trace).
5) Lightweight acceptance tests + canary plan doc for SRE handoff.

Wireframe writeups (notes to designers/devs):
- Route list (compact row): name | model pin | qps | avg-latency | actions.
  - Model pin is a pill with caret. Hover reveals: pinned model id, last pin time, small "Change pin" button.
- Route edit panel -> right rail: Fallbacks & Rollouts panel.
  - Top: radio group: Off | Manual only | Auto fallback (with thresholds).
  - Below: a horizontally scrollable chip list for fallback candidates. Each chip has model name, region flag, est-cost delta. Chips reorder by preference.
  - Bottom: Rollout tripwire block: threshold inputs (error rate %, window minutes), action (rollback | switch-to-next-fallback).
- Confirmation modal when changing pin: shows 3 quick datapoints: estimated cost delta (30d), recent latency change (median), risk tags (breaking-changes). Primary CTA: Save + Schedule (immediate | midnight | canary percent).

Backlog groom / cut decisions (why we cut or keep):
- Keep: Fallback selection UI (critical to unblock several CS requests).
- Keep: Model pin quicktoggle (high impact, small surface).
- Keep: Rollout tripwire (low surface, high safety).
- Cut: Multi-tenant policy editor (scope creep).
- Cut: Full cost simulation engine (expensive).
- Cut: Auto-suggest fallback based on perf (future; needs data infra).

Rough estimates (T-shirt):
- UI + small API (fallback UI + save): 4 dev days frontend + 2 backend days + 1 day QA.
- Pin quicktoggle: 2 dev days frontend + 1 backend + 0.5 QA.
- Tripwire: 1 backend day + 0.5 frontend + 0.5 QA.
- Observability links: 1 dev day (console) + 0.5 integration.
Total: ~2.5 dev-weeks across 3 engineers (parallelizable).

Acceptance criteria (must pass to merge):
- Route edit: user can add up to 3 fallback entries and save them to the route config.
- If auto-fallback enabled, server returns a rollout config and tripwire with threshold fields present.
- Pin change modal shows cost delta when backend returns estimate (if estimate fails show "estimate unavailable").
- Canary: ability to schedule pin change at 5% traffic for 1 hour.
- Observability links open the correct trace context in logs UI.

Dependencies & constraints:
- Backend: extend route config schema to include fallbacks array + tripwire object (schema change reviewed in CON-1524).
- Auth: RBAC checks for pin changes (must re-use existing role checks).
- Data: cost estimate endpoint needs minor extension (already in API but rate-limited).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: auto-fallback accidentally routes sensitive traffic to hosted (data leak).
  - Mitigation: for Private deployments default auto-fallback = off; show clear warning and require explicit confirmation.
- Risk: errors during quick pin change could cause config divergence.
  - Mitigation: schedule atomic config write + audit log; add post-change verification job.

Open questions (needs decision before devs start):
- Should fallback chain allow the same model in a different region? (Prefer yes, but confirm with infra about routing keys).
- What SL threshold values should we expose as sensible defaults? (Proposal: 3% errors in 5m, latency > 2x p50 for 5m).
- Does billing team want to be notified when a route falls back to hosted? (Tagging for followup with finance).

Action items (owners):
- Ava: finalize default thresholds and add to CON-1524 (due 2026-09-04).
- Ravi: implement backend schema change + small api (JIRA-9876) (start 9/07, PR by 9/10).
- Lin: prototype wireframe and handover to frontend (deliverables by 9/06).
- Priya: coordinate SRE for canary plan + test harness (due 9/09).
- Marco: add observability quick links and trace jump integration (PR by 9/11).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive and conservative. Were trying to unblock customers asking for safer, visible rollouts without building a full policy DSL. Keep the scope narrow.
- If there are objections to the safety defaults, raise them now; otherwise we will proceed with the defaults above and treat them as editable later.

Historical context / why now:
- Several Dedicated pilots have paused on aggressive pins due to lack of automated rollback (support tickets in Aug showed 27% of routing incidents tied to rollout mistakes).
- Quick wins here reduce churn and provide a surface for future features (policy marketplace, cost-sim).

Appendix (UX micro-copy suggestions):
- Fallback toggle tooltip: "When enabled, traffic is automatically redirected to the next fallback candidate when the routes performance breaches the tripwire threshold. Recommended for non-sensitive routes."
- Confirmation modal headline: "Change model pin for route “{routeName}”"
- Tripwire help text: "A tripwire temporarily pauses a rollout and/or rolls back a pin when the configured error or latency thresholds are exceeded."

Bottom line: small, tactical sprint to introduce explicit fallback chains, safer pin changes, and a tripwire safety net. Low-risk, high-customer-impact.
